fact: Vipeoples reports that Senegal's ECOWAS biometric identity card is produced under a contract with a Malaysian firm, with bill 21/2026 amending the founding law before the National Assembly on 29 September 2026.

Senegal's DAF director Ibrahima Dieng said national identity-card production resumed after the February 2026 cyberattack and that the databases used to produce national identity cards are available, intact and unchanged.
APS reports the DAF announced that national identity card production resumed on 1 April 2026 and enrolment restarted progressively in several centres, after a halt from a 5 February cyber-attack.
Senegal's national biometric ID system, implemented by IRIS Corporation from late 2016, had issued biometric IDs to more than 7 million citizens by IRIS's account.
Senegal's ECOWAS biometric ID card is in circulation, with card production resumed from 1 April 2026 after a cyberattack on the DAF and about 700,000 cards due for renewal, per the interior minister.
Bill 21-2026 amending the law that instituted the ECOWAS biometric identity card, to extend validity of cards in circulation, was sent back to committee by the National Assembly.
IPRES requires Senegalese pensioners to hold their ECOWAS national identity card to complete its proof-of-life campaign from 1 July 2026.
Access to the e-Senegal platform, launched 24 March 2026 by SENUM SA, rests on authentication with the Numero d'Identification Nationale (NIN) carried on the biometric identity card, per Ndarinfo.
RTS reports that more than 10 million citizens are enrolled biometrically.
